title: Suitability, Appropriateness and Product Governance
summary: How firms should understand their clients and products before advising, managing portfolios or selling complex instruments, and how supervisors test the quality of advice and distribution.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How firms should understand their clients and products before advising, managing portfolios or selling complex instruments, and how supervisors test the quality of advice and distribution.
Learning Objectives: Explain suitability, appropriateness and client categorisation requirements
Assess the quality of advice files and portfolio management suitability reviews
Evaluate product governance, target market and conflicts in distribution
Syllabus: File reviews: testing suitability reports and advice quality
Product governance: manufacturer and distributor obligations and target market
Conflicts of interest and inducements in advice and distribution
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for brokers, investment advisers, portfolio managers and other investment firms
Market surveillance, market infrastructure and issuer disclosure staff
Policy specialists, team leaders and heads of department responsible for securities markets
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising investment firms or securities markets is helpful. No trading or quantitative background is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
IOSCO, Regulatory Issues Raised by Changes in Market Structure (2013)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
